signature: SUBROUTINE DLASWLQ( M, N, MB, NB, A, LDA, T, LDT, WORK,

params.name: M
params.reference: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.

params.name: N
params.reference: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge M \ge 0$.

params.name: mb
params.reference: The row block size to be used in the blocked QR. $M \ge \mathrm{MB} \ge 1$

params.name: nb
params.reference: The column block size to be used in the blocked QR. $\mathrm{NB} > 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, the elements on and below the diagonal of the array contain the N-by-N lower triangular matrix L; the elements above the diagonal represent Q by the rows of blocked V (see Further Details).

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,M)$.

params.name: T
params.reference: dimension (`LDT`, N \* Number\_of\_row\_blocks) where Number\_of\_row\_blocks = CEIL((N-M)/(`NB`-M)) The blocked upper triangular block reflectors stored in compact form as a sequence of upper triangular blocks. See Further Details below.

params.name: ldt
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array T. $\mathrm{LDT} \ge \mathrm{MB}$.

params.name: lwork
params.reference: The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \mathrm{MB} \, M$. If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

sets: CALL DGELQT( M, N, MB, A, LDA, T, LDT, WORK, INFO)

untranslated: check -8.rowMajor: the column count of T is not established
